title: Empress Dowager Cixi
summary: Cixi (1835-1908) became a concubine of the Xianfeng Emperor around 1851 and bore a son in 1856. In 1861 she and Empress Ci'an overthrew the regents, and she ruled as regent for the rest of her life, according to National Geographic. In 1898 she reasserted control over the Hundred Days' Reform. She died in November 1908.

uncertainty.note: Sources give 1835-1908; EBSCO gives death as 15 November 1908, National Geographic as November 1908, one day after Guangxu.

as_recorded.value: On November 15, 1908, Cixi died at the age of seventy-two
Cixi died in November 1908, only one day after Guangxu

where.modern_name: Beijing, China (proxy pin: the capital where she ruled; her birthplace is not given in the sources)

importance.justification: Dominated the Qing court as regent from 1861 until her death in 1908.

sources.title: Cixi, the controversial concubine who became queen

reviewer_note: Sources differ: EBSCO says Cixi installed Guangxu after Tongzhi died in 1874; National Geographic's timeline lists Guangxu at age three in 1875. EBSCO does not mention the 1861 coup; National Geographic does. National Geographic says many believe she poisoned Guangxu; not asserted here. Pin is a proxy (Beijing).
